podcast.title: 60s Psychedelia Tribute
podcast.body: The Dukes of Stratosphear was XTC's pseudonymous project, conceived in 1985 to indulge their fascination with 1960s psychedelia. They adopted fake names for all band members and their producer, allowing them to experiment with a retro sound inspired by bands like Pink Floyd, The Byrds, Jefferson Airplane, Revolver-era Beatles, and The Beach Boys, purely for enjoyment and a break from their serious pop songs. "XTC wanted to try something a little retro, stuff that was outside their normal post-punk quirkiness."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: If That Is Your REAL Name

podcast.title: Producer John Leckie's Pseudonym
podcast.body: The producer for The Dukes of Stratosphear's albums was credited under the fake name Swami Anand Nagara. This was actually John Leckie, who later went on to produce The Stone Roses. "The producer was somebody named Swami Anan Nagara, and that was actually John Lucky, the guy that would later go on to produce the stone roses."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: If That Is Your REAL Name

xref.title: Producer John Leckie
xref.body: The Stone Roses were later produced by John Leckie, who had previously worked under the pseudonym Swami Anand Nagara while producing The Dukes of Stratosphear, the pseudonymous project of XTC. "that was actually John Lucky, the guy that would later go on to produce the stone roses."
